title: Pakistan Faces Accusations of War Crimes as Baloch Activists Seek International Intervention Over Soorab Bombardment
excerpt: Rights groups condemn Pakistani airstrikes in Balochistan that allegedly killed 30 civilians, as media blackout prevents independent verification of the escalating conflict.
body:
• Baloch activists have shared videos alleging Pakistani military airstrikes killed 30 civilians in the Soorab area of Balochistan, calling it a war crime and seeking U.S. intervention
  • Pakistan launched airstrikes after the Balochistan Liberation Army claimed it killed 32 security personnel in coordinated attacks
  • Rights body Paank condemned the bombardment and called for an independent international probe, while reports indicate Pakistan imposed a media blackout to conceal the scale of casualties
  • The violence marks a sharp escalation in a decades-long separatist insurgency in Pakistan's largest but least populous province

Airstrikes Draw War Crime Allegations

Baloch human rights activists have accused Pakistani military forces of committing war crimes in Balochistan's Soorab district, sharing graphic video footage that allegedly shows the aftermath of airstrikes that killed at least 30 civilians. The activists have called on the United States and the international community to intervene, according to reports in The Times of India.

The alleged strikes came after the Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) claimed responsibility for coordinated attacks that it said killed 32 Pakistani security personnel. Pakistan's military responded with airstrikes and ground operations across multiple districts in the restive southwestern province.

Media Blackout Prevents Verification

Reports indicate that Pakistan has concealed the scale of casualties through a media blackout in the affected areas. Independent journalists and humanitarian organizations have been unable to access the Soorab area to verify either the military's claims or the activists' allegations.

Paank, the human rights department of the Baloch National Movement, condemned the Soorab bombardment and called for an independent international investigation. The rights body said targeting civilians under the guise of counter-insurgency represents a serious breach of both domestic and international law.

Separately, the Baloch Voice for Justice called for a probe into what it described as the Giddar bombing, questioning Pakistan military's narrative about the operations, according to The Tribune.

A Decades-Long Conflict Escalates

Balochistan, Pakistan's largest province by land area but its least populous, has been gripped by a separatist insurgency for decades. The BLA, the region's strongest insurgent group, has intensified operations in recent months, carrying out coordinated attacks on security installations, infrastructure projects, and military convoys.

In July 2026, a wave of militant attacks across three separate areas killed 42 security personnel and four civilians, prompting Pakistan to launch Operation Shaban — a multi-district counter-insurgency campaign that the military said killed 129 militants. In February 2026, coordinated BLA attacks across a dozen locations killed at least 50 people, including 33 civilians and 17 security personnel.

International Pressure Building

International human rights organizations have documented a pattern of extrajudicial killings, enforced disappearances, and indiscriminate use of force in Balochistan. Amnesty International has repeatedly called on Pakistan to end punitive crackdowns on Baloch protests and respect the right to peaceful assembly.

Pakistan maintains that the BLA operates as a proxy of India and receives support from Afghanistan — allegations both New Delhi and Kabul deny. Islamabad says its military operations target only terrorists and their infrastructure, and are carried out in self-defense.

What's Next

The escalating cycle of insurgent attacks and military reprisals shows no signs of abating. With Pakistan rejecting calls for independent investigations and imposing information blackouts, the international community faces growing pressure to push for accountability and civilian protection in the troubled province.
nri_angle: The Balochistan crisis has direct relevance for the Indian diaspora given India's strategic interest in the region and Pakistan's accusations of Indian involvement
